quote: We now investigate a first-order stochastic dominance property satisfied by the HLIL distribution, according to the concept described in [19]. Let φ1 = (α1, λ1, β1) and φ2 = (α2, λ2, β2). Then, if α2 ≤ α1, λ1 ≤ λ2 and β1 ≤ β2, we have F(x; φ1) ≤ F(x; φ2). (7) The proof of (7) is given in the Appendix. Thus, under the considered configuration on φ1 and φ2, the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ1 first-order stochastically dominates the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ2.

quote: Also, we can use this result to show that, for β ∈ (0, 1], the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ = (α, λ, β) first-order stochastically dominates the IL distribution with parameter vector (α, λ). Such property is not immediate for the case β > 1.
